arxiv-2108-02277.title: The Primitive Ideal Space of Groupoid C ∗ C^{*} -Algebras for Groupoids with Abelian Isotropy
arxiv-2108-02277.creator: Daniel W. van Wyk, Dana P. Williams
arxiv-2108-02277.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniel W. van Wyk, Dana P. Williams. We study the topology of the primitive ideal space of groupoid C ∗ C^{*} -algebras for groupoids with abelian isotropy. Our results include the known results for action groupoids with abelian stabilizers. Furthermore, we obtain complete results when the isotropy map is continuous except for jump discontinuities, and also when G G is a unit space fixing extension of a proper groupoid by an abelian group bundle.

arxiv-2110-05389.title: A Practical Framework for Quantum Error Mitigation
arxiv-2110-05389.creator: Zhenyu Cai
arxiv-2110-05389.description: Abstract Quantum error mitigation is expected to play a crucial role in the practical applications of quantum machines for the foreseeable future. Thus it is important to put the numerous quantum error mitigation schemes proposed under a coherent framework that can highlight their underlying connections while providing guidance for their practical performance.

arxiv-2112-05516.title: Algebraic Properties of Subquasigroups and Construction of Cryptographically Suitable Finite Quasigroups
arxiv-2112-05516.creator: V.A. Artamonov, Sucheta Chakrabarti, Sharwan K. Tiwari, V.T. Markov
arxiv-2112-05516.description: Abstract In this paper, we identify many important properties and develop criteria for the existence of subquasigroups in finite quasigroups. Based on these results, we propose an effective method that concludes the nonexistence of subquasigroup of a finite quasigroup, otherwise finds its all possible proper subquasigroups. This has an important application in checking the cryptographic suitability of a quasigroup.

arxiv-2206-13854.title: The problem of calculating the β \beta -Bogoliubov coefficient in Non-Oscillating models
arxiv-2206-13854.creator: Jaume de Haro, Llibert Aresté Saló
arxiv-2206-13854.description: Abstract The calculation of the Bogoliubov coefficients is a key piece to obtain the reheating temperature of the Universe. In all cases this calculation is performed either in toy models where some derivative of the potential is discontinuous at some points or by making some approximations to the model.

arxiv-2207-11307.title: Non-Markovian modeling of non-equilibrium fluctuations and dissipation in active viscoelastic biomatter
arxiv-2207-11307.creator: Amir Abbasi, Roland R. Netz, Ali Naji
arxiv-2207-11307.description: Abstract Based on a Hamiltonian that incorporates the elastic coupling between a tracer and active particles, we derive a generalized Langevin model for the non-equilibrium mechanical response of active viscoelastic biomatter. Our model accounts for the power-law viscoelastic response of the embedding polymeric network as well as for the non-equilibrium energy transfer between active and tracer particles.

arxiv-2207-14582.title: An isoperimetric result for an energy related to the p p -capacity
arxiv-2207-14582.creator: P. Acampora, E. Cristoforoni
arxiv-2207-14582.description: Abstract In this paper, we generalize the notion of relative p p -capacity of K K with respect to Ω \Omega , by replacing the Dirichlet boundary condition with a Robin one. We show that, under volume constraints, our notion of p p -capacity is minimal when K K and Ω \Omega are concentric balls.

arxiv-2307-11621.title: On the Complexity of the Bipartite Polarization Problem: from Neutral to Highly Polarized Discussions
arxiv-2307-11621.creator: Teresa Alsinet, Josep Argelich, Ramón Béjar, Santi Martínez
arxiv-2307-11621.description: Abstract The Bipartite Polarization Problem is an optimization problem where the goal is to find the highest polarized bipartition on a weighted and labelled graph that represents a debate developed through some social network, where nodes represent user’s opinions and edges agreement or disagreement between users.

arxiv-2308-15679.title: The porous envelope and circumstellar wind matter of the closest carbon star, CW Leonis Volume: 370 Journal: Winds of Stars and Exoplanets
arxiv-2308-15679.creator: Hyosun Kim 1, Ho-Gyu Lee 1, Youichi Ohyama 2, Ji Hoon Kim 3, Peter Scicluna 4, You-Hua Chu 2, Nicolas Mauron 5, Toshiya Ueta 6
arxiv-2308-15679.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hyosun Kim 1, Ho-Gyu Lee 1, Youichi Ohyama 2, Ji Hoon Kim 3, Peter Scicluna 4, You-Hua Chu 2, Nicolas Mauron 5, Toshiya Ueta 6. Recent abrupt changes of CW Leonis may indicate that we are witnessing the moment that the central carbon star is evolving off the Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) and entering into the pre-planetary nebula (PPN) phase.

arxiv-2506-19345.title: Distributed Interview Selection for Stable Matching in Large Random Markets
arxiv-2506-19345.creator: Richard Cole, Pranav Jangir
arxiv-2506-19345.description: Abstract In real-world settings of the Deferred Acceptance stable matching algorithm, such as the American medical residency match (NRMP), school choice programs, and various national university entrance systems, candidates need to decide which programs to list. In many of these settings there is an initial phase of interviews or information gathering which affect the preferences on one or both sides.

arxiv-2509-25639.title: Model Predictions for the 2025 October Draconid Outburst 2025
arxiv-2509-25639.creator: Auriane Egal, Paul Wiegert, Danielle E. Moser, Peter G. Brown, Margaret Campbell-Brown
arxiv-2509-25639.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Auriane Egal, Paul Wiegert, Danielle E. Moser, Peter G. Brown, Margaret Campbell-Brown. The October Draconid meteor shower, produced by comet 21P/Giacobini–Zinner, is notorious for rare but intense outbursts, some exceeding rates of ∼ \sim 10 4 meteors per hour. In 2025, Earth will encounter young trails ejected by the comet in 2005 and 2012, producing a meteor outburst and providing a rare opportunity to probe their structure and benchmark meteoroid stream models.

arxiv-2511-22493.title: HW-GNN: Homophily-Aware Gaussian-Window Constrained Graph Spectral Network for Social Network Bot Detection
arxiv-2511-22493.creator: Zida Liu, Jun Gao, Zhang Ji, Li Zhao
arxiv-2511-22493.description: Abstract Social bots are increasingly polluting online platforms by spreading misinformation and engaging in coordinated manipulation, posing severe threats to cybersecurity. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have become mainstream for social bot detection due to their ability to integrate structural and attribute features, with spectral-based approaches demonstrating particular efficacy due to discriminative patterns in the spectral domain.

pmc-10628212.title: Prognostic and immunotherapeutic significance of immunogenic cell death-related genes in colon adenocarcinoma patients
pmc-10628212.creator: Jun Xu, Jun Yang, Xianzhu Pan, Jian Wang
pmc-10628212.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In recent years, genes associated with immunogenic cell death (ICD)-related genes have garnered significant interest as potential targets for immunotherapy. As a frontier in cancer treatment, immunotherapy has notably enhanced the therapeutic outcomes for cancer patients. However, since only a subset of patients benefits from this treatment approach, there is an imperative need for biomarker research to enhance patient sensitivity to immunotherapy. Expression of ICD-related genes and clinical patient data were sourced from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database.

pmc-10734395.title: Mean Platelet Volume to Lymphocyte Ratio: A New Biomarker Predicting Response in Patients with Solid Tumors Treated with Nivolumab
pmc-10734395.creator: Hasan Cagri Yildirim, Fatih Kus, Deniz Can Guven, Ece Karaca, Yunus Kaygusuz, Omer Dizdar, Sercan Aksoy, Mustafa Erman, Suayib Yalcin, Saadettin Kilickap
pmc-10734395.description: IntroductionAlthough immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are widely used in cancer treatment, identifying factors that predict treatment response remains a challenge in clinical practice. There is a need for biomarkers to identify patients who may not benefit from these treatments. It is crucial to identify a simple and cost-effective biomarker that can be easily incorporated into clinical practice.

pmc-11384696.title: Characterization of age-associated inflammasome activation reveals tissue specific differences in transcriptional and post-translational inflammatory responses
pmc-11384696.creator: Sarah Talley, Tyler Nguyen, Lily Van Ye, Rasa Valiauga, Jake DeCarlo, Jabra Mustafa, Benjamin Cook, Fletcher A White, Edward M Campbell
pmc-11384696.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Aging is associated with systemic chronic, low-grade inflammation, termed ‘inflammaging’. This pattern of inflammation is multifactorial and is driven by numerous inflammatory pathways, including the inflammasome. However, most studies to date have examined changes in the transcriptomes that are associated with aging and inflammaging, despite the fact that inflammasome activation is driven by a series of post-translational activation steps, culminating in the cleavage and activation of caspase-1.

pmc-11549558.title: Compiling a versatile toolbox for inducible gene expression in Methanosarcina mazei

Methanosarcina mazei is a model organism, providing a platform to explore methanoarchaeal regulation mechanisms on the transcriptional and translational level. pmc-11682846.title: The Surgical Odyssey: A Case Report on Rare Isolated Abdominal Wall Recurrence in an Adult Ovarian Granulosa Cell Tumor

pmc-13669230.title: CausalCellInfer: Prioritizing Cell‐Type‐Specific Disease Associations From Genetically Predicted Transcriptomes in Biobank Cohorts
pmc-13669230.creator: Liangying Yin, Yujia Shi, Ruoyu Zhang, Yong Xiang, Jinghong Qiu, Pak‐Chung Sham, Hon‐Cheong So
pmc-13669230.description: Integrating single‐cell RNA sequencing(scRNA‐seq) with the phenotypic depth of population‐scale biobanks is essential for elucidating the cellular basis of complex diseases. However, this is hindered by limited scRNA‐seq sample size and the lack of cellular resolution in biobanks. We present CausalCellInfer, a scalable computational framework bringing cellular resolution to bulk and genotype‐imputed transcriptomes.
